text: I have worked at the same animal hospital for six years. A clinic ten minutes from my house offered me $4 more an hour and better hours, but my contract says I cannot work within 25 miles for two years. I turned it down. I support the ban. Nobody should have to choose between a raise and getting sued.

I built my own client list over nine years. When I wanted to rent a chair and go out on my own, the salon owner reminded me of the noncompete I signed when I was 19. I don't even know if it would hold up, but I can't afford a lawyer to find out. So I stayed. That is what these agreements really do. They keep you scared.

I run a seven-person heating and cooling company. Every good technician in this county is tied up by the two big outfits and their noncompetes. I can't hire experienced people, so I train apprentices from scratch. Please finalize the rule. Small shops like mine are the ones it would help most.

We spend months training each engineer on systems and customer accounts that took us years to build. A narrow, reasonable non-compete is how a company our size protects that investment from a competitor that can outbid us on salary. A categorical ban treats every agreement as abusive. I oppose the rule as written and ask the Commission to exempt agreements with highly paid technical staff.

When the health system bought my practice, my contract came with a non-compete covering every hospital within 40 miles. If I leave, my patients lose their doctor. Several of them have asked me where I will go and I am not allowed to tell them. Non-competes in medicine hurt patients, not just doctors.

I make $19 an hour and I have a non-compete. I am not a scientist or an executive. There are no trade secrets in a warehouse. My raises have been 2% a year for four years because they know I can't go to the distribution center across the highway. Ban them.

I wanted to start a small landscaping supply business after I left my sales job. My former employer sent a letter saying my non-compete covered the whole state for three years. I had savings, a business plan, and two customers ready. I went back to working for someone else.

Our members support limits on non-competes for low-wage workers, and several states have already adopted such limits. We urge the Commission to adopt a salary threshold instead of a categorical ban, and to leave agreements made in the sale of a business untouched. Companies also need some way to protect client relationships that took years to build.

submitter_type: Individual (teacher at a private tutoring center)
text: My employer makes us sign a non-compete even though I have read that California does not enforce them. Most of my coworkers don't know that. They think they will be sued if they tutor on the side. Whether or not it is legal, the paper does its job.
